The **2014–15 Missouri State Lady Bears basketball team** represented **Missouri State University** in NCAA Division I women’s basketball during the **2014–15 season**. They competed in the **Missouri Valley Conference** and played home games at **JQH Arena** in Springfield, Missouri.

## Basic profile

- **School:** Missouri State University  
- **Team nickname:** Lady Bears  
- **Season:** 2014–15  
- **Conference:** Missouri Valley Conference  
- **Head coach:** **Kellie Harper**  
- **Coach’s season:** 2nd season at Missouri State  
- **Home arena:** **JQH Arena**  
- **Location:** Springfield, Missouri  
- **Final record:** **18–15 overall**  
- **Conference record:** **13–5 MVC**  
- **Postseason:** Women’s National Invitation Tournament — first round  

## Coaching staff

The team was led by **Kellie Harper**, a former Tennessee Lady Vols point guard who had previously coached at Western Carolina and NC State before taking over Missouri State. This was her second year with the Lady Bears.

Her staff around this period included members of what became a notable Missouri State coaching group, including **Jackie Stiles**, the legendary former Lady Bear and NCAA women’s basketball scoring star, who served as an assistant coach.

## Season summary

The 2014–15 Lady Bears had a strong Missouri Valley Conference season, finishing **13–5 in league play** and positioning themselves among the better teams in the MVC.

Missouri State was not the league champion that season; **Wichita State** was the dominant MVC team and won the conference tournament. The Lady Bears, however, were competitive enough to earn a postseason berth in the **WNIT**.

Their season ended in the **first round of the 2015 WNIT**.

## Missouri Valley Conference context

The Missouri Valley Conference in 2014–15 included programs such as:

- Missouri State
- Wichita State
- Drake
- Northern Iowa
- Indiana State
- Illinois State
- Southern Illinois
- Evansville
- Bradley
- Loyola Chicago

Missouri State was one of the stronger teams in the league that season, though Wichita State was the team that ultimately claimed the MVC’s NCAA tournament bid.

## Notable players

Some key Lady Bears from this era included:

### **Tyonna Snow**
One of Missouri State’s most important players. Snow was known for her athleticism, defense, steals, and all-around play. She became one of the defining players of the Kellie Harper era at Missouri State.

### **Kenzie Williams**
A major contributor and one of the team’s top scoring options. Williams was an experienced guard who helped lead the backcourt.

### **Liza Fruendt**
Fruendt was a younger player during this period and later became one of Missouri State’s standout scorers. She would go on to have a very productive Lady Bears career.

### **Lexi Hughes**
Another guard who was part of the Lady Bears’ rotation and contributed on the perimeter.

### **Aubrey Buckley**
A frontcourt player who was part of the program during this stretch.

## Style of play

Under Kellie Harper, Missouri State teams generally emphasized:

- Guard play
- Defensive pressure
- Transition offense
- Competitive rebounding
- Aggressive perimeter defense

With players like **Tyonna Snow**, the Lady Bears had the ability to create turnovers and turn defense into offense.

## Postseason

Missouri State earned a berth in the **2015 Women’s National Invitation Tournament**, commonly known as the **WNIT**. The Lady Bears were eliminated in the first round.

Even though they did not make the NCAA tournament, the WNIT appearance was an important step for the program as it rebuilt under Harper.

## Program significance

The 2014–15 season was part of Missouri State’s rise back toward national relevance under Kellie Harper. The Lady Bears had been a historically strong women’s basketball program, especially during the Jackie Stiles era, and Harper’s teams helped restore postseason expectations.

A few years later, Missouri State would return to the NCAA tournament and make a major run, including a **Sweet Sixteen appearance in 2019** under Harper. The 2014–15 team was one of the building blocks toward that success.

## Quick facts

| Category | Detail |
|---|---|
| Team | Missouri State Lady Bears |
| Season | 2014–15 |
| Head coach | Kellie Harper |
| Conference | Missouri Valley Conference |
| Overall record | 18–15 |
| MVC record | 13–5 |
| Home arena | JQH Arena |
| Postseason | WNIT first round |
| Key players | Tyonna Snow, Kenzie Williams, Liza Fruendt, Lexi Hughes |

In short, the **2014–15 Missouri State Lady Bears** were a competitive MVC team in Kellie Harper’s second season, finishing **18–15**, going **13–5 in conference play**, and earning a **WNIT berth**. They were led by a core that included **Tyonna Snow** and **Kenzie Williams**, with younger players such as **Liza Fruendt** beginning to emerge.
